messages:
incident-bot: [ALERT] Spike in 5xxs on POST /v1/chat (regions: us-east1, eu-west). Error rate ~12% over 8m, p95 latency up. Paging on-call.

lia (oncall): I'm on it. Quick glance shows error distribution skewed to 503s and 504s from gpu-runtime-pool. Traces show many long-lived streaming connections with repeated prefix fetches.

omar (runtime): Confirmed. KV cache eviction churn looks correlated with many concurrent streams holding large contexts. Also seeing bursty retry loops from a handful of API keys. Suspect client-side massive parallelism + aggressive client retries.

lia (oncall): Immediate mitigations I propose: 1) apply temporary tenant-level concurrency cap for top offenders (soft throttle). 2) lower server-side per-process streaming concurrency cap from 6 -> 2. 3) push urgent SDK guidance to reduce parallel streams and change retry defaults to decorrelated jittered backoff. I'll authorize infra to apply caps.

tess (eng-infra): Using infractl to set quota cap:

```
# soft throttle top tokens to 3 concurrent streams, 8 rps
infractl quota update --token <TOKEN> --concurrency 3 --rate 8 --scope streaming --mode soft
```

Staging on us-east1 and eu-west now.

lia (oncall): Thanks. Devex, can you draft the short SDK advisory and code snippets we can paste to customers/support? Keep it actionable.

devex: Drafting now. Key points: limit concurrent streaming connections per process, use idempotency header X-Idempotency-Key for any retriable mutate requests, and switch to decorrelated jitter backoff. Suggest default params: initial=300ms, cap=8000ms, max_attempts=5. Also recommend client-side short idle close for streams after 20s. 

Sample JS snippet (hotfix):

```
// set decorrelated jitter backoff
const policy = {
  baseMs: 300,
  maxMs: 8000,
  attempts: 5,
  jitter: 'decorrelated' // implement jittering per rand between prev and cap
};
client.configureRetries(policy);

// idempotency header
await client.chat.create({ prompt: '...' }, { headers: { 'X-Idempotency-Key': uuidv4() } });

// reduce concurrency
client.streaming.defaults.maxParallel = 1;
```

Python example:

```
from redwood import Client

c = Client(api_key=KEY)

c.retries.set(base_ms=300, max_ms=8000, attempts=5, jitter='decorrelated')

c.chat.create('...', headers={'X-Idempotency-Key': f"txn-{uuid4()}"})

c.streaming.max_parallel = 1
```

omar (runtime): Also note: prefer short-lived streams for high-throughput workloads. If a customer batches payloads, switching to chunked non-stream POSTs reduces long-lived socket pressure.

nina (support): I'll prepare a customer-facing blurb: "We're throttling a small set of noisy clients while we stabilize. Recommended immediate actions: update SDKs to the hotfix, reduce parallel streams, and add idempotency keys. Contact support if you need help." Will send to affected accounts after infra confirms caps applied.

lia (oncall): Tess, please confirm when the soft caps are live. Also flip the runtime feature flag to lower global streaming concurrency.

tess (eng-infra): Caps live in us-east1 and eu-west. Running monitoring checks. Applying runtime flag now:

```
infractl feature set --service streaming --key max_concurrency --value 2
```

Rollout should be within 45s.

omar (runtime): Seeing traffic shape already. Errors dropped to ~3.5% within a minute, p95 latency improved ~30%. Tenants with caps show immediate request rate drop.

lia (oncall): Good. Next actions: 1) Devex publish SDK hotfix and notify support. 2) Add temporary telemetry tag to incoming requests to identify client versions holding many streams. Tess, can you enable client-version tagging?

tess (eng-infra): Enabling lightweight header tag capture (header: X-Client-Stream-Tag) via feature flag.

lia (oncall): Sam (next oncall), you'll take handoff in 30m. I'll prepare a short handoff note: which tokens were capped, commands used, and current metrics baseline.

sam (next-oncall): Acknowledged. Please include list of capped tokens in the PD incident record and ensure support has the customer list so we can coordinate SDK adoption. I'll monitor for 2h.

nina (support): Sent initial note to affected customers. Including steps and timelines. Asking for confirmation once they've applied hotfix.

omar (runtime): Follow-up: we've held caps for 18m; overall error rate stable ~0.8%. I recommend gradually relaxing soft caps only once we see SDK uptakes or customers confirm changes.

lia (oncall): Agreed. I'll keep caps in place and monitor. If metrics remain stable for 30m we can reduce global override further. Handing off to Sam now. TL;DR: noisy clients caused streaming concurrency and KV cache thrash -> applied per-tenant soft caps + reduce global streaming concurrency -> metrics improved -> push SDK hotfix for backoff, lower concurrency, idempotency headers.

sam (next-oncall): Taking over. Will shadow dashboards and coordinate rollback/relaxation based on customer updates. :thumbsup:
